title: Tiffani Faison to close Sweet Cheeks Q and Fool’s Errand in the Fenway
author: Nathan Tavares
bullets: Tiffani Faison announced the closure of her Fenway restaurants Sweet Cheeks Q and Fool's Errand later this year.
Sweet Cheeks Q will end operations on November 24, marking nearly 15 years since its opening.
Faison cited rising costs and unsustainable restaurant environments as reasons for not renewing leases.

title: Take a look inside New Hampshire’s oldest continuously operated inn after a makeover
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: The Inn at Hancock in New Hampshire, established in 1789, reopened in May after a three-year, multi-million dollar renovation.
Renovations were led by Kerri Landry and Jeffrey Delvy, emphasizing history with bold colors and luxurious details.
The inn offers three suite types, locally sourced dining, and is located near popular activities like skiing and mountain climbing.

title: Acton teen accused of killing mom, brother ordered held without bail
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Arjun Aravind, 17, is accused of murdering his mother and brother in Acton; ordered held without bail after arraignment.
Prosecutors noted violent struggle signs; victims suffered blunt force trauma. Aravind was arrested in Wayland after a manhunt.
Aravind allegedly used ChatGPT for violent story creation; will undergo mental health evaluation, next court date is Sept. 11.

title: Downtown Boston was buzzing in July. Here’s a look at the numbers.
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Downtown Boston's foot traffic increased by 10.5% in July 2026 compared to the same month in 2025, says Downtown Boston Alliance.
Events like the World Cup, Sail Boston, and new social districts contributed to a 40% sales boost for Temple Place businesses.
Boston City Council is considering extending bar hours after successful pilot increased downtown activity and economic growth.

title: 2 seriously injured in West End stabbing, police say
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Two individuals were seriously injured in a stabbing incident on Lancaster Street in Boston's West End.
The injuries occurred in a domestic incident; man's injuries were self-inflicted and life-threatening, woman's not life-threatening.
Boston Police encourage tips to the Homicide Unit or anonymous line as the investigation continues.

title: Healey temporarily restricts kratom sales statewide
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Massachusetts temporarily classifies kratom as a Schedule I substance, citing high abuse potential and lack of medical use.
The order grants local officials power to enforce restrictions on kratom sales, effective after a 14-day notice.
Massachusetts joins other states in restricting kratom, with varying regulations across New England.

title: Two New England beach towns to visit before the summer ends
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Harwich, Massachusetts was voted best town on Cape Cod by Boston.com readers, offering beaches and sunset cruises.
Ogunquit, Maine named best beach town in New England, features charming scenery and travel tips from Boston.com.
The Deerfield Fair, New England's oldest family fair, is set for Oct. 1-4 in Deerfield, New Hampshire.

title: Diver dies in incident off Cape Cod
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 72-year-old man died in a diving accident off Cape Cod near Sesuit Harbor on Wednesday.
The Dennis Fire Department and other multiple agencies conducted a coordinated search after the diver went missing.
The diver was located and pronounced dead around 5:30 p.m.; the incident is under investigation.

title: Lindsay Clancy’s raw journal entries read in court
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Prosecutors requested access to visitor logs for Lindsay Clancy during her trial, focusing on visits from a forensic psychologist and a priest.
Trooper Joshua McKelligan testified about the crime scene and Clancy's medications, revealing her husband's involvement in managing prescriptions.
Lindsay Clancy's journal entries revealed struggles with postpartum depression and anxiety, expressing a desire to be a present and happy mother.

title: Rhode Island beach house with water views on both sides — can you guess the price?
author: Emily Turner
bullets: The Rhode Island beach house is located in Westerly and features water views on both sides.
Built in 1987, the house is a contemporary cottage with 2,724 square feet, 3 bedrooms, and 3 full baths.
The 2025 property taxes are $11,125, and it has a private sewer and public water supply.
